description: A push that LANDS on a protected branch (master, production-*) is the operator's call, including a push that names no branch at all.
_on_error_why: Fails closed: when git cannot say where a push goes (an unknown flag, a variable, a GIT_* override, a git that fails or hangs), refusing costs one retry and allowing can cost master.
_match_why: Needs the push_destination engine (HAG-53); an older engine rejects the unknown matcher and, with it, the whole policy file. Pair it with protected-branch-push (the regex rule), placed first: that one needs no git and covers subtree push and send-pack; this one resolves what the regex cannot see - bare git push, git push origin, git push origin HEAD from master, push.default upstream/matching, remote.<name>.push, remote.pushDefault - by asking git in the repo the push runs in (after -C and cd). Git is run only for a git push, and only because this rule exists. A dry run is not a destination. Errors (on_error decides): an unknown flag, a variable, brace expansion, an inline alias, a GIT_DIR/GIT_CONFIG_*/HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME override, env with an option, a git that fails or runs past the 3-second deadline. NOT COVERED: pushd, a subshell's cd leaking into a later command, an alias defined in git config or the shell, a script file, and an environment the agent's shell exported earlier that the harness does not share.
reason: That push lands on a protected branch (master or production-*), which is the operator's call. Push a feature branch (git push -u origin HEAD from a feature branch) and open a PR with bb pr create instead.
